main_text.p: cumque amatoribus ita versa-ri, non est citra infamiæ no-tam; & muliebris illa nuditas, quâcunque de causâ sit institu-ta,semper erit reprehendenda.

Quid quod nulla sit ratio, quæ desumpta à validâ generatio-ne,ab incitamento ad nuptias, à patriæ defensione. Cum er-jam principium generationis in fœminis satis validum sit fu-turum, si exercitiis validis, li-cet non sint nudatæ vacare in-cæperint. Nec minorem in bel-lo operam præstabunt, etsi ve-stitæ semet exerceant. Neque enim vulgare auxilium ma-tro æ Germanæ maritis mili-tibus teste Cæsare præstiterunt[?], utriusque fortunæ sociæ comi-tes, licet nunquam inter illas exercitium nudarum fuerit ad-missum. Quod verò spectat conciliationes nuptiarum, di-cendum illam concertationem nudam, non tam incitare ad nuptias,

page.notes: The words "nudam" and "non" in the last lines are set in a heavier, different typeface than the rest of the page; I have marked them as black letter, but this is uncertain. "præstiterunt" is hard to read at the line end; the mark is doubtful. The long s is printed as f throughout and is transcribed as s (e.g. "verfa" as "versa", "fit" as "sit", "fpectat" as "spectat"). Faint text at the lower right edge is outside the printed page and has been left out.
